text: Thank you for the information; I will treat this as your initial presentation of increasing right knee pain and swelling, urinary pain, and a history of a self-resolving left ankle joint. To understand the severity and potential cause, do you have a fever, and is the right knee warm or red to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome). 

The clinical triad of a history of migratory asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle followed by right knee), urethritis (pain with urination), and recent onset in a sexually active male is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis, likely triggered by an undisclosed preceding infection (e.g., Chlamydia). The family history of rheumatoid arthritis is a distractor.
